upstream_diff.hypothesis: Without a real AIC, no device interrupts reach the guest, so drivers like AppleSEPManager never complete probing and never publish their IOKit service; ACMTRM then times out waiting for it.

decisive_finding.finding: ACMTRM/SEP timeout is NOT the actual root-shell blocker. The upstream darwin-vm root shell comes from a PATCHED ramdisk containing a com.jprx.bash launchdaemon, an iOS sysroot, and a custom trustcache built on macOS via hdiutil + codesign (get_files.sh patch_ramdisk). Our Windows fixture uses the RAW unpatched ramdisk, so iOS runs the restore daemon instead of bash. The upstream AIC source comment itself states: you do not need a working AIC to boot to a root shell.

ab_experiment.hypothesis: Real Apple AIC interrupt controller would unblock AppleSEPManager probing
ab_experiment.result: REJECTED — serial output 33,052 vs 33,060 bytes, same terminal state, same ACMTRM timeout. AIC alone changes nothing for this milestone.
ab_experiment.method: Cherry-picked hw/intc/apple_aic.c + apple_aic.h + meson + darwin.c wiring from upstream bad6336 onto pinned 2867d847; rebuilt; ran identical 60s serial gate

upstream_pipeline.windows_gap: No APFS ramdisk mount/patch/codesign pipeline exists on Windows yet. The Phase 4 vphone-udif-win / vphone-aea-win / apfs_snapshot tooling covers container decode but not full APFS LaunchDaemons replacement + ad-hoc signing + trustcache rebuild.
upstream_pipeline.get_files_sh: patch_ramdisk() mounts ramdisk.dmg with hdiutil on macOS, replaces /System/Library/LaunchDaemons with com.jprx.bash.plist, extracts ios_sysroot.tar.gz, ad-hoc codesigns all binaries, and builds ramdisk.tc from their cdhashes
upstream_pipeline.conclusion: Reaching a guest root shell on Windows requires porting the ramdisk patching pipeline (or obtaining a pre-patched ramdisk), not additional SEP/AIC device emulation for this milestone.
